newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ZAGALO HITS OUT AT BARCELONA INTERFERENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAGALO HITS OUT AT BARCELONA INTERFERENCE.

text.p: Mario Zagalo slammed Barcelona on Monday for carrying the Ronaldo transfer saga into the heart of his Brazil team as they prepared to face the hosts in the opening match of the Tournoi de France.
"Transfers ought to be hathe city concerned and not in the heart of the Brazilian national team," Zagalo said after the world champions practised at Lyon's Gerland stadium, venue of Tuesday's match.

"The Brazilian team must not be affected by a problem that is not theirs," he said as an off-colour Brazil look for a big improvement on their shock 4-2 defeat to Norway in a friendly in Oslo last Friday.

World footballer of the year Ronaldo, in the middle of a tug of war between Barcelona -- for whom he played this season -- and Internazionale of Milan, looked as if his mind was anywhere but on the pitch during the evening practice.
Asked if Ronaldo was perturbed, Zagalo said: "Everyone would like to be perturbed with millions of pesetas in their hands."
Ronaldo was quoted in France on Sunday as saying "all doors to Barca are closed."
After Monday's practice he said: "This is not the place to discuss the transfer. I want to concentrate on tomorrow's game.
"I will decide where to play next season when Barcelona have decided (what they want)," he added, confusing the issue.
Zagalo said it was not the first time Barcelona had affected his squad's concentration over the 20-year-old striker who scored 34 goals for the Spanish giants this season.
He recalled transfer talk going on when Brazil were involved in the 1996 Olympic Games soccer tournament with Ronaldo in the middle of his move from PSV Eindhoven to Barcelona.
"We need more comprehension from the Barcelona directors. They are constantly coming to bring problems into the national team," Zagalo said.
Zagalo is bolstering his defence by bringing back World Cup veteran Aldair of Roma, who looked sharp in a defence put through their paces by a mobile reserve attack in the practice.
